dashboard.gainTotal.explain: Your total gain is the sum of four terms — unrealised gain, realised gain, dividends received, and the fees your broker takes out of your transfers. That sum is its definition: the app adds the four up rather than computing a total separately and trusting that they agree. The fourth term belongs to no security, which is why a table of positions can never show it.
dashboard.ytd.pending: history not rebuilt that far back yet
dashboard.ytd.noPreviousYear: nothing recorded before 1 January, so there is no year to count from yet
dashboard.netContributed.explain: Net contributed: your deposits less your withdrawals, fees excluded. It is the silent denominator of both returns, and the reason the total gain has a fourth term — a fee taken from a transfer leaves your cash without lowering what this figure records.
dashboard.xirr.explain: Money-weighted return: what your deposits actually earned. It is the single annual rate that reconciles everything that entered and left, each on its own date, with what the portfolio is worth today — so money paid in before a rise weighs more than money paid in after it. Returns are computed from the dates of your events.
dashboard.twr.explain: Time-weighted return: how the positions themselves performed, independent of your deposits. Paying money in, or taking it out, moves it by nothing at all, which is what makes two portfolios of different sizes comparable. It depends on the period it covers, and a ranking can reverse inside it. Returns are computed from the dates of your events.
dashboard.awaitingCurrency: Your total value, your net contributions and both returns are waiting for a reporting currency — nobody has answered that question yet.
dashboard.withoutLedger: A ledger of dated events would add your total value, your net contributions and both returns.
dashboard.empty.title: No events yet
dashboard.empty.body: Everything here is computed from a ledger of dated events. Nothing has been imported or entered yet.
shares.gainTotal.explain: The gain of every line of this table, closed positions included — their realised gain and their dividends stay in this figure long after the position itself is gone, and leaving them out would show you a second figure, just as correct, that is not your gain. It is the sum of the three columns below, which is what makes it checkable by eye. One term cannot appear here: the fees your broker takes out of a transfer belong to no security.
shares.value.explain: What you hold, converted into your reporting currency. A position whose price has never been observed is counted at what it cost rather than at zero — the app does not invent a quote, and the em dash in the price column is what says so.
shares.unrealised.explain: Unrealised gain: what a position is worth today less what it cost you. It moves with the market and it is not money you have; carried at cost, a position with no observed price shows exactly zero rather than a loss.
shares.realised.explain: Realised gain: what your sales actually brought in, net of the fees on them and of the cost of the shares that left. It is a decomposition of your total gain and never a term to add to it — the proceeds are already in your cash.
shares.dividends.explain: Dividends received on this position, since the first event of your ledger. Fees taken on a payment are already deducted, and a position keeps this figure after it is sold.
shares.avgCost.explain: The unit cost of what you still hold, computed as the weighted average of your acquisitions with the fees on them absorbed — the French tax convention, and the app carries no other. A sale removes shares at that average and leaves it unchanged, so a closed position has no unit cost at all.

data.form.create.title: A new event
data.form.edit.title: This event
data.form.description: A portfolio is a ledger of dated events: say what happened, then when and how much.
data.form.date.explain: Returns are computed from the dates of your events. Both of them read the dates recorded here, and neither can tell a date you were sure of from one you estimated — so if you no longer have it, record your best estimate and read those two figures knowing that.
data.form.date.unreadable: Nothing is recorded without a readable date: write it as YYYY-MM-DD. A date field erases what it could not read, and says nothing about it.
data.form.grantPrice.explain: Left empty, the award is a dilution: it adds shares and nothing else — nothing paid in, nothing it cost you. Filled, the value you declare feeds both at once: the shares enter your contributions and your cost basis together, so the position starts with no unrealised gain rather than with a gain equal to its whole value.
data.form.required: This kind of event needs this field.
data.empty.file.title: Drop a file
data.empty.file.body: Put a .csv or an .xlsx of your events into the import folder. The app reads it by itself, whatever it is called, and a file covering one year only is a legitimate start.
data.empty.manual.title: Enter a first event
data.empty.manual.body: A position is typed as the events that built it — a purchase, its date, its price. If you no longer have the date, record your best estimate.
installation.settings.imposed.note: These are read when the app starts and cannot be answered from here. Changing one means recreating the container.
installation.settings.imposed.default: not set, the app's own value
installation.settings.saved: {count, plural, one {# setting saved} other {# settings saved}}. {now, plural, =0 {No share was re-armed} one {# share was re-armed} other {# shares were re-armed}}; {later, plural, =0 {none others are waiting for a market to open} one {# other will read the new value when its market opens} other {# others will read the new value when their markets open}}.
installation.settings.unchanged: Nothing had moved, so nothing was written.
installation.settings.refused: The app refused these values and wrote none of them.
settings.regular_interval.hint: How often a share whose market is open is asked for its price.
settings.backfill_interval.hint: How often the historical rebuild takes its next step.
settings.backfill_delay.hint: A courtesy to the price source, at the moment the app asks it the most.
settings.backfill_chunk_days.hint: How much history one rebuild request covers.
settings.staleness_horizon.hint: How long a stored price may stay frozen while the market moves before it is reported. 0 turns the check off.
settings.base_currency.hint: The one currency every figure is reported in. It is fixed from your first recorded event, and changing it later would reinterpret your amounts rather than convert them.
settings.cadence.reach: Saving this applies to {now, plural, one {# share} other {# shares}} now, and to {later, plural, =0 {none others} one {# other when its market opens} other {# others when their markets open}}.
settings.backoff.retroactive: A share the app has failed to price waits a multiple of this number before it is tried again, so changing it rescales that wait retroactively — including for a share that has been failing since this morning.
installation.store.persistence: {state, select, persistent {This path is on a mount that outlives the container.} ephemeral {This path is inside the container and is lost when it is recreated.} other {Whether this path outlives the container cannot be observed here.}}
installation.store.ephemeral.title: This container keeps nothing
installation.store.ephemeral.body: The store sits in the container's own writable layer, so everything you record disappears the next time it is recreated. That is a fine way to try the app out. To keep it, mount a volume on this path and start it again.
installation.store.size.note: Purging returns rows, not bytes: the store reuses its own blocks, so this figure does not go down when something is removed from it.
installation.store.orphans: {count, plural, one {# share nothing declares any more} other {# shares nothing declares any more}}
installation.store.orphans.body: Their price history was kept when their events left, because forgetting an import can be undone by dropping the file again and a rebuilt history cannot. A position you have sold is not one of these — its events are still recorded.
problem.storageUnavailable: The data cannot be read right now. The app is running, its store is not answering.

problem.unreachable: The app is not answering. Nothing on screen comes from it.
